findings.title: TypeScript release signer and repository references retain the Rust repository target
findings.decision: confirmed by coordinator and independent skeptic
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The TypeScript release cannot use its supported signing/publication path until repository routing is corrected.

reproduction.method: Independent static trace and inspection of coordinator-retained evidence; public data only.
reproduction.entryAndInput: node scripts/sign-release.mjs v0.2.0 --publish --dry-run; static COMMANDS inspection.

findings.expected: Release lookup, download, attestation, upload and optional publication target hobby-eng/mnemocode_typescript.
findings.observed: The retained dry run routes every repository-specific gh command to hobby-eng/mnemocode. The constant is unchanged between the initial and current snapshots. No release was signed, uploaded or published.
findings.impact: The supported TypeScript publication procedure addresses the Rust repository. It can fail to find the intended draft; if a same-tag compatible draft exists there, the commands remain directed to that other project. No wrong artifact signature or attestation bypass was demonstrated.
findings.severityRationale: Medium supported build/release routing failure; the concrete wrong command plan justifies blocking TypeScript publication. High severity is unsupported without an executed integrity failure.
findings.recommendedFix: Correct the TypeScript repository target and stale current TS help/security/download/provenance links. Preserve the intentional opening README link recommending the Rust version. Keep historical audit evidence unchanged.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify the corrected dry-run plan for download/attestation/upload/publish and relevant no-publish/refusal cases. Inspect current TS references and preserve the deliberate Rust link. Do not create a real release as a test.
findings.core54Assessment: Reachable external input/OS failure or ordinary successful-path ownership omission; no trusted intrinsic/runtime failure injected or required.

findings.title: Digestless omission diagnosis mistakes majority agreement for evidence against one share
findings.decision: confirmed by coordinator and independent skeptic
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Bounded diagnostic defect for imported threshold-one sets. No automatic digest-checked phrase is emitted by this diagnosis; phrase-only recovery still refuses digestless results and downstream warnings remain. MnemoCode does not create threshold-one sets.

reproduction.input: Independently CRC-framed public imported 1-of-3 values A,A,B with distinct members, all six permutations; checked 2-of-3 damaged-share control.

findings.expected: Without a digest-checked restored reference, preserve unchecked disagreement without identifying a particular wrong share.
findings.observed: All six actual permutations return trouble.kind=odd/code=share-does-not-fit at the minority B place (3,2,3,2,1,1), despite the equal A,A reference having digestChecked=false. Real checked 2-of-3 control correctly identifies damaged share 3. Probe exits 1; no stop or source drift.
findings.impact: Recovery advice can tell a person to leave out the correct minority copy after correlated corruption of the majority. No automatic digest-checked phrase is returned by the failing diagnosis, and later digestless recovery remains labelled/refused by the phrase-only API.
findings.severityRationale: Medium supported recovery-diagnosis error: majority agreement of unauthenticated imported shares can cause a person to discard a correct minority copy. This is stronger than a cosmetic label issue. Limited import scope, required user action and preserved digestless warnings justify no release block. No secret theft, automatic correct-share deletion or authenticated wrong recovery was shown.
findings.recommendedFix: Only count a successful omitted-share subset as identifying an outlier when its restored reference is digestChecked. Preserve non-attributing disagreement otherwise.
findings.requiredVerification: Preserve all six digestless permutations without named odd-share attribution, equal digestless sets with explicit unchecked state, grouped threshold-one cases and checked 2-of-3 outlier behavior. Trace ShareRestore/CLI propagation and keep operational host failures distinct.
findings.core54Assessment: Real imported shares, independent CRC and ordinary WASM; no trusted native/runtime method is mocked or required to fail.

findings.title: Direct MissingCodes.run accepts malformed external check answers as passing codes
findings.decision: confirmed by coordinator and independent skeptic
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Bounded impact; no additional release block justified under current audit rules.

reproduction.method: Independent static trace and inspection of coordinator-retained evidence; public data only.
reproduction.entryAndInput: Public direct MissingCodes.run API, english/direct, abandon x11 plus about|abandon; externally supplied callback returns {matched:false} or the string false.

findings.expected: The external host callback must return a boolean; malformed answers are refused before they can establish a passing candidate.
findings.observed: Retained source-entry probe: false => count 1/passed 0/kept 0; true => 1/1/1; both {matched:false} and string false => 1/1/1. Probe exits 1 for two accepted malformed answers.
findings.impact: A malformed JavaScript host integration can receive a false pass. Shipped MissingCodesSearch callbacks produce booleans and wallet paths validate through askWallet; no supported CLI false recovery was shown.
findings.severityRationale: Low direct-host contract defect. CORE-54 trusts the program's own typed results, not data returned by an external host service. Validation belongs only at that external boundary; it cannot verify an intentionally dishonest boolean checker.
findings.recommendedFix: Refuse non-boolean awaited answers at the direct public boundary, retaining valid booleans, cancellation and ownership behavior.
findings.requiredVerification: Keep false/true controls, sync/async malformed answer refusals, result disposal and late-stop semantics through the actual public entry. Do not inject native faults.
findings.core54Assessment: Reachable external input/OS failure or ordinary successful-path ownership omission; no trusted intrinsic/runtime failure injected or required.

findings.title: Interactive filename retries bypass regular-file admission and can block cancellation
findings.decision: confirmed by coordinator and independent skeptic
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Bounded impact; no additional release block justified under current audit rules.

reproduction.method: Independent static trace and inspection of coordinator-retained evidence; public data only.
reproduction.entryAndInput: POSIX FIFO with no writer entered at the Record file name retry after an unreadable initial decode file.

findings.expected: Interactive filename admission refuses a non-regular file promptly, preserving cancellation; explicit headless material streams remain a separate supported contract.
findings.observed: The real PTY control common-input route exits 130 after SIGINT. The retry-file route remains running for the two-second wait and is ended by the probe-owned group cleanup. Static QR retry/next-share routes use the same blocking reader default; those variants were not separately reproduced.
findings.impact: A person selecting a FIFO or link to one can stall the local interactive recovery session, including its JavaScript SIGINT cleanup. No remote denial of service, secret disclosure or ordinary regular-file failure was shown.
findings.severityRationale: Low bounded local availability/cancellation failure. This is an OS file-kind trigger, not an injected failure of openSync.
findings.recommendedFix: Apply the existing regular/nonblocking descriptor policy at interactive text and QR filename boundaries without removing intentionally supported explicit headless streams.
findings.requiredVerification: Actual PTY: text retry FIFO, QR retry and next-share FIFO, regular-file success, directories/devices, links and Ctrl+C. Keep limit/limit+1 streaming regressions separate.
findings.core54Assessment: Reachable external input/OS failure or ordinary successful-path ownership omission; no trusted intrinsic/runtime failure injected or required.

findings.title: Failed redirected stdout export reports successful process completion
findings.decision: confirmed by coordinator and independent skeptic
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Bounded impact; no additional release block justified under current audit rules.

reproduction.method: Independent static trace and inspection of coordinator-retained evidence; public data only.
reproduction.entryAndInput: Protected encode --mode direct --format unicode --mnemonic-file - with public zero-entropy phrase and stdout on Linux /dev/full.

findings.expected: A refused output write produces an observable nonzero failure rather than successful export completion.
findings.observed: The retained /dev/full CLI run returns status 0, signal null, and only expected fingerprints on stderr. Independent OS control gets ENOSPC; normal stdout control returns 0 and the expected 105-character public output. The defect harness itself exits 1.
findings.impact: A script can accept a missing/incomplete redirected backup as successfully emitted. No original phrase was deleted, file overwritten, wallet changed, or secret compromised in this example.
findings.severityRationale: Low export defect with bounded demonstrated impact. Supported I/O failure is real, but Medium data-loss language would overstate evidence without automatic destruction of the only source or a stronger mandatory persistence guarantee.
findings.recommendedFix: Propagate real standard-output write failures through command completion, with meaningful stderr and terminal cleanup. Keep expected broken-pipe policy explicit if relevant.
findings.requiredVerification: Real OS failed output plus ordinary pipe/file output controls, process status and cleanup. Exercise affected result writers through the shared policy; do not mock intrinsic write methods.
findings.core54Assessment: Reachable external input/OS failure or ordinary successful-path ownership omission; no trusted intrinsic/runtime failure injected or required.

findings.title: Mixed share conversion leaves ordinary mutable working copies unwiped
findings.decision: confirmed by coordinator and independent skeptic
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Bounded impact; no additional release block justified under current audit rules.

reproduction.method: Independent static trace and inspection of coordinator-retained evidence; public data only.
reproduction.entryAndInput: Normal mixed-form share reads/writes, e.g. colorsToShare on the retained public SSKR vector.

findings.expected: Program-owned mutable working copies of a share or a reversible representation receive one best-effort wipe after use under CORE-24/TS-07.
findings.observed: mixShare creates an unmixed full body; ownUnitCount creates packed bytes; mixedTransport creates an unmixed body; mixedToShare creates sliced units and packed bytes. They are not transferred as live results and have no local wipe. Wiping only the final transport does not wipe these separate allocations.
findings.impact: Avoidable share-bearing mutable copies are abandoned for GC. This establishes missing source-level cleanup, not a measured surviving heap pattern, cross-process disclosure or guaranteed JavaScript erasure failure.
findings.severityRationale: Low normal-path cleanup/conformance defect, statically established without failed fill/set operations. Existing owner disposal and immutable-string limitations do not excuse these owned local copies.
findings.recommendedFix: Give temporary arrays explicit ownership and one finally cleanup attempt, or pack only the header when that is all the caller needs. Preserve borrowed arrays and live returned results.
findings.requiredVerification: Review normal successful/refused public mixed reads/writes, literal six-form results and caller-input preservation. Passive temporary ownership evidence is sufficient; no synthetic trusted-native faults or broad heap claims.
findings.core54Assessment: Reachable external input/OS failure or ordinary successful-path ownership omission; no trusted intrinsic/runtime failure injected or required.

findings.title: Native split drops its copied interpolation result without a zeroizing owner
findings.decision: confirmed by coordinator and independent skeptic
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Bounded impact; no additional release block justified under current audit rules.

reproduction.method: Independent static trace and inspection of coordinator-retained evidence; public data only.
reproduction.entryAndInput: Normal native Shamir split with threshold at least two and a generated interpolated share.

findings.expected: The temporary share-bearing Vec is wiped once after copying or held by a zeroizing owner under CORE-24/RUST-13.
findings.observed: interpolate returns Result<Vec<u8>>; the loop binds v, copies v into result_item, then drops ordinary Vec v without memzero or a zeroizing owner. Later memzero calls cover digest/x/y, not v.
findings.impact: Source-level best-effort cleanup omission for a generated share copy. Whether optimized canonical WASM allocates or retains it after return remains unmeasured; no post-call memory leak is asserted.
findings.severityRationale: Low source-conformance finding, rather than the hypothesis's unproved residual-memory allegation. The same narrow evidentiary standard accepts C02: ordinary successful-path temporary ownership is enough to show that no cleanup attempt was requested.
findings.recommendedFix: Zeroize/own the interpolation temporary or avoid the redundant copy in separately authorized vendor remediation, retaining canonical build procedure.
findings.requiredVerification: Inspect success ownership and share literals; targeted native regressions and canonical regeneration only when remediation is authorized. Binary/assembly evidence is required only for stronger retained-memory claims.
findings.core54Assessment: Reachable external input/OS failure or ordinary successful-path ownership omission; no trusted intrinsic/runtime failure injected or required.

findings.title: Heir-sheet renderer lets an unbreakable host subtitle extend outside the page
findings.decision: confirmed by coordinator and independent skeptic
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Bounded impact; no additional release block justified under current audit rules.

reproduction.method: Independent static trace and inspection of coordinator-retained evidence; public data only.
reproduction.entryAndInput: Supported HeirRoute with subtitle W repeated 100 times; ordinary encoded/direct 12-word facts; real node renderer, A5 and A6.

findings.expected: A successful printable guide keeps host text on paper or explicitly refuses unsupported width.
findings.observed: Actual two-page PDFs retain one 100-identical-glyph Tj line. Actual font advance and placement give A5 right edge 769.923605 versus page width 419.527559 pt; A6 607.434947 versus 297.637795 pt. Both return success; clippedDocuments=2 and the harness exits 1.
findings.impact: A supported host can receive a recovery instruction sheet with text beyond the page. Standard CLI route was not affected by this fixture; no backup code corruption or confidentiality failure is established.
findings.severityRationale: Low host-provided layout defect; actual PDF operators/geometry establish overflow without claiming a pixel or physical-print acceptance run.
findings.recommendedFix: Break/scale/refuse over-wide single tokens before returning a successful sheet, preserving ordinary routes and vertical limits.
findings.requiredVerification: A5/A6 actual generated PDF bounds for long subtitle/step/address, ordinary routes, vertical fit and supported font coverage. Preserve caller-owned output and input.
findings.core54Assessment: Reachable external input/OS failure or ordinary successful-path ownership omission; no trusted intrinsic/runtime failure injected or required.

caveats: Four scoped ledgers cover 653 distinct paths: 635 full semantic/static text reads, two exhaustive numeric-data parses, two partial/structural native texts and 14 binary metadata/hash-only paths. Every current src path has an owner; numeric world-map data and protection flag JSON are not ordinary algorithm source.

The remaining 666 paths belong to the coordinator, including one newly added workflow. coverage.json states actual full or selected current-tool/document reads and structural-only historical review; no claim of semantic review of all archived reports/harnesses.

All 84 package exports map to reviewed source owners (54 core/root, 15 cards, 15 SSKR). Token inventory finds 2,770 declarations/methods; it is not a full TypeScript AST, exhaustive invocation inventory or branch-coverage measure.

rows.text: If the problem could expose, alter, or incorrectly recover secret material, report it privately through [GitHub private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/hobby-eng/mnemocode/security/advisories/new) instead of opening a public issue.
> **This TypeScript version is complete and takes fixes of critical defects only.** MnemoCode continues in Rust: use the Rust version, [hobby-eng/mnemocode](https://github.com/hobby-eng/mnemocode).

Report a suspected vulnerability privately through the [GitHub private vulnerability reporting form](https://github.com/hobby-eng/mnemocode/security/advisories/new) of this repository. The report goes to the repository owner and maintainers. Do not describe an unfixed security problem in a public issue, discussion, pull request, screenshot or log.

Ordinary defects and feature requests belong in the [public issue forms](https://github.com/hobby-eng/mnemocode/issues/new/choose). If publishing a report could help an attacker or reveal recovery material, report it privately.

The project has automated tests and dated audit records. It has not had an independent security audit by cryptography specialists. The Rust library behind the Shamir shares describes itself as being under community review; the external audit of the C version does not cover it. The [source layout](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) and the [audit records](https://github.com/hobby-eng/mnemocode/tree/main/docs/audits) describe the limits of the program; they are not a security certificate.

Download MnemoCode from its release page, `https://github.com/hobby-eng/mnemocode/releases`, and from nowhere else. Choose the file for your computer: the one ending in `win-x64.exe` for Windows, `macos-arm64` for a Mac with an Apple processor, `linux-x64` for Linux.

The signing computer needs the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/) with the `gh attestation` command, logged in (`gh auth login`) with the right to edit releases of `hobby-eng/mnemocode`; GnuPG with the release key; and `sha256sum`. The release key's fingerprint:

Standalone pre-release verification is complete for the three tested native targets. The full [CI run](https://github.com/hobby-eng/mnemocode/actions/runs/39722442871) checked signed source `f980236`; all three source-test and real-terminal jobs passed. No confirmed high/medium code finding remains open in the reviewed release paths. This is bounded verification, not a claim that every possible defect or CORE violation has been ruled out.

The full Linux job also passed mandatory code/duplication/dead-export/type/lint gates, Rust tests and doctests, build, full self-test, PDF/image/QR export, independent SSKR known answers and the standard dependency audit, which reported no known vulnerabilities. The runtime source, native engine, dependencies, assets, embedded manual/vectors and executable-build inputs remain byte-identical to the three accepted [native executable jobs](https://github.com/hobby-eng/mnemocode/actions/runs/39719696645) at `2e8c249`. Those executables were built and tested on their own OS, including empty-folder execution and real terminal checks; their source identity is preserved rather than relabeled as a later rebuild. The Linux artifact also matches the two local builds byte for byte.

- The `SHA256SUMS` of every release is signed with the maintainer's OpenPGP key, fingerprint `28FC51B1DB80DF2101128CB30EDD4814591DD095`, which GitHub also shows at https://github.com/hobby-eng.gpg. A tag creates a draft release, which the maintainer checks and signs on their own computer with `scripts/sign-release.mjs` before publishing it with `SHA256SUMS.asc` and `RELEASE-SIGNING-KEY.asc`; [Releasing](https://github.com/hobby-eng/mnemocode/blob/v0.1.0/docs/RELEASING.md) describes the steps.
- The README gives an overview. The [command-line reference](https://github.com/hobby-eng/mnemocode/blob/v0.1.0/docs/CLI.md) holds the command examples and every option.

- `recover-word`, `recover-date` and `sskr-combine` save their candidates with `--candidates-file` as a [candidate list](https://github.com/hobby-eng/mnemocode/blob/v0.1.0/docs/CANDIDATES.md) for the Discovery Scanner of the multi-chain wallet tools: encrypted with age to the one-time key the Scanner shows, or with a passphrase; without encryption only with `--plaintext-candidates`. Entry 6 of the menu offers it. The search, the list and its encryption are host-neutral modules that the Wallet Deriver and the Scanner compile unchanged.

- `encode --heir-sheet` saves one sheet for heirs, to print on both sides in A5 or A6 (`--heir-sheet-size`): what the backup is, room for a hint written by hand, the steps in the menu, and the basics for someone new to wallets. It holds no secret: no codes, no dates, no fingerprint and no places. [A guide for heirs](https://github.com/hobby-eng/mnemocode/blob/v0.1.0/docs/HEIRS.md) explains the same in more detail.

- Each part of the library, such as the date search, the share set or the wallet check, has an entry point of its own without Node.js code, such as `mnemocode/core/date-search`. Another program, a browser page for example, takes only the part it needs and passes what only it has, such as its PBKDF2 or its SSKR library. A long search, or the assessment of a share repair, stops at the host's signal and gives what it found before the stop, marked as stopped, rather than failing. [Source layout](https://github.com/hobby-eng/mnemocode/blob/v0.1.0/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#modules-for-other-hosts) lists the parts.

hypothesisDisposition: SSKR-H01: six fresh actual-WASM public Unicode/ASCII cases left none of the selected public share-text window in linear memory after return/refusal. Hypothesis not reproduced, no finding. This bounded negative check is not universal erasure proof.

SSKR-H02: source cap of 256 hidden coordinates identified, but no supported concrete valid fixture with an independently complete expected candidate set was established. Unresolved hypothesis, not a finding or known omitted recovery result.
SSKR-H03 was narrowed to AUD-039-SEC002: ordinary source-level absence of a cleanup owner only. Post-return binary residue remains unproved.

Failures requiring trusted fill/set/DataView/Drop/runtime operations to fail were excluded under CORE-54. Trusted installed-code/manifest substitution and hostile pre-initialization are trust-model limits, not malformed-share attacks.
No automatic digest-checked false phrase, arbitrary secret disclosure, remote execution or high/critical bug was established by these probes.
